acceptance_criteria.criterion: The workspace-detail notes textarea has appropriate sizing and spacing.
The notes view renders as a two-panel layout with sidebar on the left.
The sidebar scrolls independently of the main content panel.
Note cards have clear visual boundaries and consistent spacing.
The save-status indicator is positioned near the textarea label.
Sidebar items with notes are visually distinct from those without.

summary: Audited and refined the CSS notes styling in gui/public/css/styles.css. The workspace-detail notes section, notes-collected two-panel layout, sidebar, and note cards were already CSS-complete from prior WPs. The one gap was AC #5: `.workspace-notes-section` used `display: flex; flex-direction: column` which placed the save-status indicator below the textarea (far from the label). Changed it to `display: grid` with a 2-column, 2-row layout: label and status share row 1 (label left, status right), textarea spans both columns in row 2. All 780 tests pass.

comments.note: gui/public/css/styles.css: The .notes-view height is `calc(100vh - var(--nav-height))` but the main `<main>` element adds 24px vertical padding on top and bottom. This can cause the two-panel layout to slightly overflow the viewport. A `padding: 0` override on the main element when the notes view is active, or changing the calc to subtract padding as well, would prevent a scroll seam. Not blocking.

gui/public/css/styles.css: The .notes-card-textarea uses `outline: none` with no visible focus substitute (only a subtle background color via color-mix). For keyboard and accessibility consistency this should match the `.workspace-notes-textarea:focus` pattern (border-color change) or add a visible focus-visible ring.

summary: All 6 AC verified. CSS grid layout on .workspace-notes-section correctly positions save-status inline with the Notes label (row 1 col 2), textarea spanning full width in row 2. Two-panel notes view has independent scroll on both sidebar and main panel. Note cards have clear borders, shadow, and 20px gap. .has-notes items show blue dot (::before) and bold font-weight. comments.note: gui/public/css/styles.css: .notes-view height is calc(100vh - var(--nav-height)) but <main> adds 24px vertical padding, which can cause a subtle overflow scroll seam. Subtracting the padding from the calc or overriding padding on <main> when the notes view is active would prevent it. Not blocking.

gui/public/css/styles.css: .notes-card-textarea uses outline: none with only a background color-mix as the focus indicator. For keyboard/accessibility consistency it should match .workspace-notes-textarea:focus (border-color change) or add a focus-visible ring. Not blocking.

summary: WP-010 PASS. Core implementation is well-executed: the grid-based `.workspace-notes-section` layout (1fr auto / auto auto) correctly places save-status inline with the Notes label while keeping textarea full-width in row 2. The two-panel notes view, independent sidebar scroll, card boundaries, and `.has-notes` indicator are all architecturally sound. Applied two Fix-Forward improvements: (1) corrected `.notes-view` height from `calc(100vh - var(--nav-height))` to subtract the 48px main element padding (consistent with the existing `#app` pattern); (2) added an inset `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--color-primary)` to `.notes-card-textarea:focus` to provide a WCAG-compliant visible focus indicator alongside the existing background change.

comments.note: gui/public/css/styles.css (.notes-view): Changed `height: calc(100vh - var(--nav-height))` to `calc(100vh - var(--nav-height) - 48px)`. The `<main>` element has `padding: 24px` (top + bottom = 48px), making the old value 48px taller than the content box, causing a scroll seam. The fix aligns with the `#app` pattern which already uses the same subtraction: `calc(100vh - var(--nav-height) - 48px)`.

gui/public/css/styles.css (.notes-card-textarea:focus): Added `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--color-primary)` to the focus rule. The textarea uses `border: none` and `outline: none`, so the existing `color-mix` background change was the only focus indicator — too subtle to satisfy WCAG 2.4.7 (Focus Visible). The inset box-shadow provides a clear primary-colour ring without disrupting the card border or layout.

[documentation-forward] The `color-mix()` CSS function used in `.notes-card-textarea:focus` requires Chromium 111+, Firefox 113+, Safari 16.2+. If the project docs list a browser compatibility matrix, add a note there. No source code change needed — it is already used elsewhere in the stylesheet.
